final.investment_thesis: The evidence that decides this is the split between a broken tape and an unbroken franchise, and the fact that the catalyst gap has already been taken. The bear legitimately won the tape argument: 2026-07-31 was a 2.6x-normal-volume (132.5M share) distribution day closing -7.35% at 308.91, below the 50-SMA (309.50) and 5.35% under the VWMA (326.39), with a bearish MACD cross and RSI 43.24 — no oversold cushion. That creates a real three-measure overhead supply shelf at roughly 324-327 (Bollinger mid 324.37 / VWMA 326.39 / 10-EMA 327.24), so near-term reward/risk into that shelf is only about +5.9% versus roughly -10% to the rising 200-SMA at 277.96. The bear also scored a genuine fundamental point on gross margin: 50.06% in FQ3 versus 46.49% a year ago (+357 bp) in a hardware-heavy mix with no segment disclosure in the dataset to source the expansion, while inventory rose $5.7B to $11.1B and raw materials 3.6x, and Cook's 'hundred-year flood' memory-pricing language argues for cost pressure flowing into COGS. A plausible ~300 bp give-back is roughly $12B after tax, ~$0.80+ of EPS, pushing the multiple from ~34x toward ~37-38x on normalized numbers. That is a real reason not to pay up, and I am not paying up. But the franchise itself is not impaired: FQ3 revenue $109.4B (+16.4%), EPS $2.02 (+28.7%), net income +27.1%, 9M operating income $122.4B (+21.7%), 9M FCF $110.2B, and $51.2B net cash with zero new long-term debt. The September guide of +9-11% is deceleration, not contraction, and management attributes it to memory supply, FX and China softness — supply-constrained guides are recoverable in a way that demand-collapsed guides are not. The primary trend is intact: the 200-SMA at 277.96 is rising and 11% below price, the 50-SMA sits 11.35% above it, and the 50-SMA breach was 0.19% — a momentum break, not a structural one. The 300 level was defended on 2.6x volume with a close +2.97% off the low and back inside the lower Bollinger Band, which is supply meeting a bid rather than a vacuum. The buyback point cuts both ways: ~$375-380 average repurchase prices are not a floor, but $62.1B of capital was deployed and net share count still fell ~1.11% while the company deleveraged — capital discipline, not distress. CEO transition (Ternus), services regulatory drag and capex-driven FCF optics are legitimate overhangs that argue for sizing discipline, not for zero. On sizing, I choose 15% now against a concrete higher 25% and a concrete lower 0-10%. The 25% full plan target today is not warranted: it would have me paying into a three-measure supply shelf +5.9% away with ATR 9.87 (3.20% of price) and MACD crossed down, the exact poor asymmetry the bear identified; 324-327 would only justify 45-50% if it were reclaimed with segment or cost-pass-through evidence, and neither exists in the supplied dataset. The 0-10% path is also not warranted: with 100% cash earning zero interest and a four-session-old ~10% flush in a business compounding EPS ~29% with a fortress balance sheet, total abstention is itself an aggressive timing bet I cannot evidence, and my own record cuts against it — the 2026-06-30, 07-01, 07-13, 07-20, 07-21, 07-22 and 07-23 AAPL Underweights all lost 3-8% of alpha within five days by trimming or refusing exposure into an intact stacked uptrend, and the 2026-07-24 Hold's entry caution paid only because a binary print was days away — that print has now occurred, so the gap-risk argument no longer applies to fresh money at 308.91. At 15% the scenario math is near-balanced: a full -10% retrace to the 200-SMA zone costs about 1.5% of total equity, while participation in a repair back to 340-344 contributes about 1.5% of total equity — which is why 15% now, not 25% and not 0-10%. This is not a tiny observation stub: 15% is ~$15,000, a genuine economic position whose contribution to account return is material in both directions; if the thesis degrades to the point where only a token holding is justified, the correct action is target_weight_now = 0, not a keepsake. The stated 25% total target is a narrative condition (reached only on a daily close above 312.66), not an order; the 300.00 no-add line, 289.36/283.78 reference zones and 277.96 invalidation are also close-basis conditions, not resting stops. Explicitly missing from the supplied evidence and not assumed: gross-margin segment disclosure, any quantification of memory cost pass-through into FQ4/FY27, FY27 guidance, post-transition CEO commentary, and news coverage for 2026-07-24 through 07-29. What would change the call: a decisive close below 300.00 halts accumulation, below 289.36 shifts me toward reducing, and a loss of the 200-SMA at 277.96 invalidates the primary-trend argument outright; conversely a close above 327.24 on above-average volume would let me raise the total target toward 30-35% because that proves the shelf has been absorbed.
